[00:27:40] **Anders Holm:** Then that is what I would do between now and October. Not buy anything. Find out whether the footprint data is in the range review pack, because if it is, you have an argument that makes itself.

[00:27:58] **Anders Holm:** Then honestly, you have another year, and you should spend it on the mill conversation rather than on us.

[00:28:06] **Tomas Hedlund:** You are quite bad at selling.

[00:28:08] **Anders Holm:** [laughter] I am extremely good at not selling to people who are not going to buy. It is the same skill viewed from the other end.

[00:29:01] **Anders Holm:** Tell him you want to know whether there is a sustainability section, because if there is you would like ten minutes of his agenda to prepare him for it. That is a request he will say yes to without thinking about it.

[00:29:29] **Tomas Hedlund:** No proposal?

[00:29:30] **Anders Holm:** Not yet. A proposal before you know the answer to those two questions is a proposal I would be making up.

[00:29:38] **Tomas Hedlund:** All right. That is reasonable. Give me a fortnight, it is holiday season and half the office is away.

[00:29:46] **Anders Holm:** A fortnight is fine. I will put something in the calendar for the week after next and you can move it if you need to.



[00:29:56] **Anders Holm:** One last thing before I let you go, and it is not a sales question. If somebody did own this properly here, what would you want them to do first?

[00:30:08] **Tomas Hedlund:** [pause] Honestly? Write down what we already know. There is a lot of it and it is in four places and one of them is my head, and if I went under a bus tomorrow the company would start from nothing.

[00:30:55] **Tomas Hedlund:** [pause] Right.

[00:31:04] **Tomas Hedlund:** [laughter] It is a very low bar. I have had four of these calls this year.

**Deal notes added by Anders Holm 2026-08-19:**

Good call. Genuinely good, and I do not say that often after a first discovery.

Industrial bakery, 180 people, crispbread and rye crisp, own brand for two chains. Two lines, fourteen real recipes, forty article numbers. Gas ovens on a single site meter, renewable electricity since 2024.

Trigger is a template from one chain, March, twelve products. He filled it in with trade association averages and a covering note saying indicative. Nobody came back. He is worried about that rather than reassured by it, which is the right instinct and is rarer than it should be.

The blocker is flour. Nearly all of the product by weight, two mills, seventy thirty, and he has no farm level data and thinks the mill does not either. He has a nineteen year relationship with the big mill which is the best possible starting position for the supplier work.

Capacity is the real constraint and he said so plainly. He is the sustainability department. One hour a week, usually Sunday. Has raised resourcing twice in management meetings and been agreed with and then ignored both times. His words: it has been not yet for two years, which at some point becomes a no with better manners.

The mechanism here is the customer, not the regulation. Their MD approves things when a customer mentions them. There is a range review with the chain in October and he had not connected it to this. That is the whole deal if the range review pack has a footprint column in it.

Did not propose. Sent him two questions instead: what does the mill hold on farm origin, and is there a sustainability section in the range review pack. Follow up pencilled for week after next, he asked for a fortnight because of holidays.

One thing I noticed and cannot do anything with. He answered every question fully and without hedging, including the ones that made his own company look disorganised, and at the end he said somebody should really own this properly here. People do not usually talk like that about a place they have been for nineteen years unless something has shifted.
